paragraphs: The fostering services shown above list Reading as an area they cover. They include Brighter Futures for Children, the not-for-profit company that runs children's services for Reading Borough Council, so fostering with it means caring for Reading's own children, alongside independent agencies.

Brighter Futures for Children's sufficiency strategy for 2024 to 2026 explains the local picture. The number of Reading children in foster care fell from 206 in 2017/18 to 176 in 2022/23, and it describes its own pool of carers as the smallest it has been. About 63% of children in foster care were living within 20 miles of Reading. Its priority is a fostering service that can care for children in Reading or as close to it as possible, and it names emergency and therapeutic foster care as gaps.

Ofsted rated the fostering service good in early 2022, an improvement on its previous inspection in 2020. In July 2024 Reading joined a fostering recruitment partnership funded by the Department for Education with other councils across the South East, and the company's board chair said Reading did not have enough foster carers living in the town. In July 2025 it launched the Mockingbird programme, which links a group of six to ten fostering families around an experienced hub carer for support.
Talk to the council's service and the agencies above about the support and pay they offer. The Berkshire and Thames Valley pages list more services nearby.
